Trades walkthrough
Wiring and circuits make electrical work the strongest task connection. Plumbing shares enough installation and work-site interests to stay on the shortlist. HVAC remains available in the full field list.
Fictional development case. Includes shared scripted defaults.

Your current interests can connect with more than one education route. A short example can help you discover whether an unfamiliar subject or way of thinking appeals to you. You can keep a hands-on or noncollege fit even when its pay does not cover your preferred lifestyle.

Other matches
Electricians Needs confirmation Your follow-up tasks support this option.
Apprenticeship
Install and repair electrical systems.
Use drawings and safety procedures to solve practical problems.
Why this matches you
Needs confirmation
Your interest profile and work choices connect with this career.
Wiring, electrical equipment and circuits
Install a new system from drawings and instructions
Different homes and buildings that need service
How you like to work
You want to build skills. Pick one skill to practise and get feedback on.
You value security. Compare paid hours, benefits, and whether the job is employed or self-employed.
You value independence. Ask which decisions a new employee makes and which need supervision.
How to get there
Texas electrician license for non-exempt work.
Start with an apprentice license and supervised work.
Journeyman: 8,000 supervised hours and exam.
Public electrical work runs through a licensed contractor.
Paid apprenticeship Austin ETA: 4 years
Work experience 8,000 hours
Qualified work Texas license + required exam
Apprentice pay comes first. Qualified electrician wages describe a later stage. College technical or business courses can add options.
Useful for moving into construction management
A construction-management degree can prepare you to manage building projects. You still need supervised work and licensing to become an electrician.

HVAC technicians Related match Shares mechanics/electronics and physical/manual labor work with Electricians.
Technical training / college courses
Install and repair heating or cooling equipment.
Find problems and help systems run well.
Why this matches you
Related match
Shares mechanics/electronics and physical/manual labor work with Electricians.
How you like to work
You enjoy working with others. Teamwork matters in this job.
You want to build skills. Pick one skill to practise and get feedback on.
You value security. Compare paid hours, benefits, and whether the job is employed or self-employed.
You value independence. Ask which decisions a new employee makes and which need supervision.
How to get there
Texas ACR technician registration; contractor license is separate.
Registered technician route starts at age 16.
Work through a licensed ACR contractor.
EPA Section 608 certification for covered refrigerant work.
Useful for learning more repair skills
Technical-college classes teach heating, cooling, and electrical systems. Business classes help with pricing and running a repair business.
Programs to explore

My saved notes and steps
Explore electrical work safely
Visit a public training demonstration or approved student program. Practice algebra, measurement, and reading diagrams. Do not work on live wiring.
My notes
Compare a paid apprenticeship and college options
Austin ETA combines four years and 8,000 hours of training. Review admission steps, published pay, tuition, tools, and Texas licensing. Compare technical college classes and construction-management study too.
My notes
Ask an apprentice and a qualified electrician
Ask about hours, travel to job sites, physical demands, tuition, and how pay changes with completed training. Ask which pay figures are that employer’s rates and which are area-wide estimates.
My notes
